description: Foreign key linking to the ABR encoding ladder profile being assigned to the channel
Foreign key linking to the broadcast channel receiving the ABR profile assignment
Identifier of the broadcast operations or encoding engineer who created this ABR profile assignment. Used for audit trail and operational accountability.

Free-text explanation of why this ABR profile was assigned to this channel (e.g., 'Upgraded to 4K for premium sports content', 'Cost optimization - reduced bitrate ladder', 'New HDR support for flagship channel').

Current lifecycle status of the assignment. Active assignments are used in production encoding; scheduled assignments will become active at effective_start_date; testing assignments are used in pre-production validation.

Estimated monthly encoding cost in USD for this channel-profile assignment, calculated based on channel broadcast hours, ABR profile complexity (rendition count, codec), and encoding farm pricing. Used for cost optimization and budget planning.
Timestamp when this assignment record was last updated.

Numeric ranking indicating the priority or preference order of this ABR profile for the channel when multiple profiles are assigned simultaneously (e.g., primary HD profile = 1, fallback SD profile = 2). Lower numbers indicate higher priority.

Quality of Service tier designation for this specific channel-profile assignment, which may differ from the ABR profile's default qos_tier. Allows per-channel QoS tuning based on content importance, audience demographics, or commercial agreements.

Foreign key linking to the broadcast channel where campaign ads will air
The actual Gross Rating Points delivered on this channel for this campaign as of the last measurement. Compared against target_grp to assess delivery performance.

The portion of the total campaign budget allocated to this specific channel. Sum of all channel allocations should equal campaign total_budget_amount.

The date when ad spots for this campaign begin airing on this channel. Must fall within campaign_start_date and campaign_end_date.
Timestamp when this channel allocation record was last modified.
The total number of ad spots contracted to air on this channel for this campaign during the flight period.
Target Gross Rating Points allocated to this channel for this campaign. Represents the reach and frequency goals specific to this channel allocation.

Foreign key linking to the broadcast channel that will air this media asset

business_glossary_term: Channel Asset Playout - Media Asset Id
description: Foreign key linking to the media asset configured for playout on this channel
Date when this asset becomes available for playout on this channel. Supports embargo management and scheduled content releases.
Date when this asset is no longer available for playout on this channel. Supports license expiration, seasonal content rotation, and rights window management.
Total number of times this asset has been broadcast on this channel. Used for rights management (license play limits), rotation analytics, and content performance tracking.
Indicates whether this asset serves as a backup/filler for this channel. Backup assets are used when primary scheduled content is unavailable or to fill unscheduled time slots.

Version identifier for channel-specific edits or adaptations of the media asset (e.g., regional edit, censored version, time-compressed version). Same base asset may have different versions per channel based on content rating, market, or time slot requirements.
Timestamp when this channel-asset playout configuration was created in the system.
Timestamp of the most recent playout of this asset on this channel. Used for rotation management to ensure content freshness and avoid excessive repetition.
Maximum number of times this asset may be broadcast on this channel within a 24-hour period. Used to prevent over-rotation and maintain content variety.
Minimum number of hours that must elapse between consecutive airings of this asset on this channel. Prevents back-to-back repetition.

Channel-specific priority ranking for this asset in automated playout rotation. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used by Ericsson MediaFirst to select assets when multiple options are available.
Current operational status of this channel-asset playout configuration. Active=available for playout, Suspended=temporarily disabled, Expired=past active_to_date, Pending=before active_from_date.
Timestamp of the most recent update to this channel-asset playout configuration.

The effective start date of the commercial carriage agreement between the channel and the OTT platform.

Indicates whether Electronic Program Guide data for this channel is synchronized to this OTT platforms EPG system. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

The logical channel number assigned to this channel specifically on this OTT platform, which may differ from the channels broadcast logical_channel_number. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

The branded channel name displayed to subscribers on this specific OTT platform, which may differ from the channels network_name for branding or licensing reasons. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

The display priority or prominence ranking assigned to this channel within this OTT platforms channel lineup, used for UI ordering and recommendation algorithms. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

The date on which this channel began or will begin simulcast distribution on this OTT platform. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

The maximum number of times the channel is permitted to broadcast this title under this license agreement. Null indicates unlimited runs.
The cumulative count of times this title has been broadcast on this channel under this license. Incremented by playout automation after each airing. Used to enforce runs_allowed limits.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country or region code defining the geographic territory where this license is valid. Enforces territorial broadcast restrictions.
System timestamp when this license record was last modified, typically when runs_consumed is incremented or license_status is changed.

Comma-separated list of dayparts where this channel actively targets this demographic segment (e.g., Prime Time, Late Fringe, Early Morning). Drives programming and ad inventory allocation decisions.
The date from which this channel-demographic targeting strategy and rate structure became effective. Typically aligned with broadcast season or upfront period start.
The date until which this channel-demographic targeting strategy and rate structure remains effective. Null indicates current/ongoing targeting. Used to track historical targeting strategy changes.
The guaranteed Gross Rating Points (GRP) committed to advertisers for this channel-demographic pairing during the upfront sales period. Drives make-good obligations if underdelivered.

Indicates whether this demographic segment is designated as a primary target demographic for this channel (vs. secondary or tertiary). Primary targets drive programming decisions and receive highest sales priority.

The pricing multiplier applied to the base CPM rate for this demographic segment on this channel. Reflects the relative value and scarcity of this audience on this specific channel (e.g., 1.25 for premium demos, 0.80 for lower-value segments).

The target rating point (percentage of demographic universe) that this channel aims to achieve for this specific demographic segment. Used in upfront guarantees and programming performance evaluation.

Current lifecycle status of this channel-demographic targeting relationship. Active indicates current targeting, Planned for future seasons, Suspended for temporary holds, Discontinued for ended strategies.
Timestamp when this channel targeting record was last modified.

business_glossary_term: Ad Pod Maximum Count Per Hour
description: The maximum number of ad pods (commercial breaks) permitted per hour within this daypart. Used by Wide Orbit for ad scheduling capacity planning and by Ericsson MediaFirst for playout rundown validation. Supports FCC commercial time compliance monitoring.
reference: FCC 47 CFR Part 73 (Commercial Limits); Wide Orbit Traffic System

description: The maximum allowable total duration in seconds for an ad pod (group of ads in a break) within this daypart. Governs commercial break length limits enforced by Ericsson MediaFirst playout automation and Wide Orbit ad scheduling. Aligns with FCC commercial time limits for children's programming dayparts.
reference: FCC 47 CFR Part 73 (Commercial Limits); SCTE-35 Digital Program Insertion; Wide Orbit Traffic System

description: Pipe-delimited list of days of the week on which this daypart definition applies, using three-letter abbreviations (e.g., MON|TUE|WED|THU|FRI for weekday dayparts, SAT|SUN for weekend). Governs schedule generation in Ericsson MediaFirst and ad inventory availability in Wide Orbit. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MON|TUE|WED|THU|FRI|SAT|SUN — promote to reference product]
reference: Nielsen Media Research Daypart Taxonomy; Wide Orbit Traffic System

description: The average audience size in thousands of viewers (000s) expected during this daypart, based on Nielsen Media Research Platform historical ratings data. Used as the principal quantitative measurement of daypart audience value for ad sales, GRP calculations, and content scheduling decisions.

The baseline CPM (Cost Per Mille) rate in US dollars for advertising inventory sold within this daypart, before application of the rate_multiplier or audience demographic adjustments. Represents the floor pricing reference used in Salesforce Media Cloud upfront and scatter market proposals.
reference: IAB Digital Video Ad Impression Measurement Guidelines; Wide Orbit Traffic System

description: Indicates whether geographic broadcast blackout restrictions can be applied to content scheduled within this daypart. When True, blackout rules (e.g., sports rights geographic exclusivity) may be enforced by the distribution platform. Aligns with must-carry and retransmission consent obligations.
reference: FCC 47 CFR Part 76 (Blackout Rules); Rightsline Rights Management

description: The maximum permissible TV content rating (per MPA/TV Parental Guidelines) for programming scheduled within this daypart. Enforces content appropriateness standards — e.g., Prime Time may allow up to TV-14, while Children's dayparts are restricted to TV-Y or TV-Y7. Used by Ericsson MediaFirst for schedule validation.
reference: Motion Picture Association (MPA) TV Parental Guidelines; FCC 47 CFR Part 73; Ofcom Broadcasting Code

business_glossary_term: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) Restricted
description: Indicates whether this daypart is subject to COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) restrictions due to programming directed at children under 13. When True, audience data collection, behavioral targeting, and ad pod duration limits are governed by COPPA compliance rules and FCC children's television regulations.
reference: COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act); FCC Children's Television Act; FCC 47 CFR Part 73

description: The timestamp when this daypart record was first created in the scheduling domain data product. Supports audit trail, data lineage tracking, and Silver layer ingestion reconciliation in the Databricks Lakehouse.
reference: SOX Section 404 (Internal Controls); GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

description: Indicates whether this daypart is eligible for Dynamic Ad Insertion (DAI) on OTT and streaming platforms. When True, ad pods within this daypart can be dynamically replaced with targeted ads during streaming delivery through Akamai CDN, enabling addressable advertising revenue.
reference: IAB Digital Video Ad Impression Measurement Guidelines; SCTE-35; Akamai CDN

description: High-level classification of the day-of-week applicability for the daypart. 'weekday' covers Monday–Friday, 'weekend' covers Saturday–Sunday, 'all_week' applies every day, and 'holiday' applies on designated public holidays. Used for rate card segmentation and audience demographic profiling.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Daypart Taxonomy; IAB Digital Video Ad Impression Measurement Guidelines

description: Short alphanumeric business identifier for the daypart, used as the externally-known reference key across Wide Orbit traffic system, Ericsson MediaFirst playout automation, and Salesforce Media Cloud ad sales. Examples: PRIME, EARLY_AM, DAYTIME, LATE_FRINGE, OVERNIGHT. Aligns with Nielsen daypart taxonomy codes.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Daypart Taxonomy; Wide Orbit Traffic System

description: Free-text narrative description of the daypart, including its programming characteristics, audience profile, and scheduling context. Used for internal documentation, Salesforce Media Cloud proposal narratives, and EPG metadata. Example: 'Prime Time (8PM-11PM) — highest-rated evening programming block targeting Adults 18-49.'

Human-readable label for the daypart segment as displayed in the Electronic Program Guide (EPG), ad sales proposals, and scheduling interfaces. Examples: Early Morning, Morning Drive, Daytime, Prime Time, Late Fringe, Overnight.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Daypart Taxonomy; IAB Digital Video Ad Impression Measurement Guidelines

description: Current lifecycle state of the daypart definition. 'active' indicates the daypart is in operational use for scheduling and ad sales. 'inactive' means temporarily suspended. 'draft' means under review before activation. 'deprecated' means retired from use but retained for historical reference.
reference: Wide Orbit Traffic System; Ericsson MediaFirst Playout

description: Classifies the daypart by broadcast delivery mode. 'linear' applies to traditional scheduled broadcast, 'non_linear' to on-demand programming windows, 'simulcast' to simultaneous multi-platform broadcast segments, and 'vod_window' to VOD availability windows governed by this daypart definition.
reference: ATSC A/65 Program and System Information Protocol; DVB-SI EN 300 468

description: Total duration of the daypart window expressed in minutes. Derived from start_time and end_time boundaries but stored explicitly for scheduling calculations, ad inventory capacity planning, and rate card generation in Wide Orbit.
reference: Wide Orbit Traffic System; Nielsen Media Research Daypart Taxonomy

description: The calendar date from which this daypart definition becomes effective for scheduling and ad sales operations. Supports versioned daypart definitions where boundaries or rates change seasonally or following regulatory updates. Used in Wide Orbit and Ericsson MediaFirst schedule generation.
reference: Wide Orbit Traffic System; Ericsson MediaFirst Playout

description: The calendar date on which this daypart definition expires and is no longer applicable for scheduling and ad sales. Null indicates an open-ended definition with no planned expiry. Supports seasonal daypart adjustments (e.g., summer schedule changes) and regulatory compliance updates.
reference: Wide Orbit Traffic System; Ericsson MediaFirst Playout

description: The clock time (HH:mm:ss, 24-hour or extended broadcast-day format) at which the daypart ends. Supports broadcast day overflow notation (e.g., 25:59:59 for content airing past midnight within the same broadcast day). Paired with start_time to define the daypart boundary.
reference: ATSC A/65; Nielsen Media Research Daypart Taxonomy; Wide Orbit Traffic System

description: The sequential display order of this daypart within the Electronic Program Guide (EPG) channel grid, used by Ericsson MediaFirst for schedule presentation and by digital EPG distribution systems. Lower values appear earlier in the broadcast day display.
reference: ATSC A/65 Program and System Information Protocol; DVB-SI EN 300 468; Ericsson MediaFirst Playout

description: The GRP (Gross Rating Point) index value representing the expected audience delivery weight for this daypart relative to the total broadcast day. Used in media planning, upfront negotiations, and scatter market pricing. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform ratings data.

The HUT (Homes Using Television) percentage representing the proportion of TV households actively viewing during this daypart. A key audience measurement metric sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform, used to benchmark daypart audience potential and inform ad pricing.

Indicates whether compensatory ad spots (makegoods) can be scheduled within this daypart to fulfill underdelivered audience guarantees from other dayparts. Governs Wide Orbit makegood scheduling logic and Salesforce Media Cloud campaign reconciliation workflows.
reference: Wide Orbit Traffic System; IAB Digital Video Ad Impression Measurement Guidelines

description: The standardized daypart code as defined by Nielsen Media Research taxonomy (e.g., PRIME, EARLY_NEWS, LATE_NEWS, DAYTIME, EARLY_FRINGE, LATE_FRINGE, OVERNIGHT). Used to align internal scheduling definitions with Nielsen audience measurement reports and ratings data ingested from the Nielsen Media Research Platform.

Pricing multiplier applied to the base CPM (Cost Per Mille) rate card for ad inventory sold within this daypart. A value of 1.0000 represents the base rate; Prime Time typically carries a multiplier greater than 1.0 (e.g., 2.5000), while Overnight may be below 1.0 (e.g., 0.3000). Used in Salesforce Media Cloud proposal generation and Wide Orbit billing.
reference: IAB Digital Video Ad Impression Measurement Guidelines; Wide Orbit Traffic System

description: Indicates whether unsold ad inventory within this daypart is available for scatter market (last-minute) sales. Governs Wide Orbit inventory availability rules for short-notice ad placement and makegood scheduling.
reference: Wide Orbit Traffic System; IAB Digital Video Ad Impression Measurement Guidelines

description: Indicates whether SCTE-35 digital program insertion cue markers are enabled for ad break signaling within this daypart. When True, Ericsson MediaFirst playout automation inserts SCTE-35 splice_insert commands at ad pod boundaries, enabling Dynamic Ad Insertion (DAI) for OTT and streaming distribution via Akamai CDN.
reference: SCTE-35 Digital Program Insertion Cueing Message for Cable; ATSC A/65

description: Indicates whether content scheduled in this daypart is eligible for simultaneous multi-platform broadcast (simulcast) across linear, OTT, and digital channels. When True, Ericsson MediaFirst can trigger simulcast distribution workflows for this daypart's programming.
reference: ATSC A/65; DVB-SI EN 300 468; Ericsson MediaFirst Playout

description: The clock time (HH:mm:ss, 24-hour format) at which the daypart begins each applicable day. Used by Ericsson MediaFirst for automated playout boundary detection and by Wide Orbit for ad scheduling slot assignment. Stored as STRING to support broadcast day conventions (e.g., 25:00:00 for post-midnight).
reference: ATSC A/65; Nielsen Media Research Daypart Taxonomy; Wide Orbit Traffic System

description: Indicates whether this daypart definition has special audience measurement and programming rules applied during Nielsen sweeps periods (intensive ratings measurement periods in February, May, July, and November). When True, enhanced content scheduling and ad pricing rules may apply.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Sweeps Measurement Periods

description: Primary audience demographic profile associated with this daypart, expressed using Nielsen standard demographic notation (e.g., A18-49, W25-54, M18-34, HH, P2+). Drives audience targeting in ad sales proposals, GRP/TRP calculations, and content scheduling decisions. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform audience measurement data.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Daypart Taxonomy; IAB Digital Video Ad Impression Measurement Guidelines

description: The IANA timezone identifier (e.g., America/New_York, America/Los_Angeles, Europe/London) governing the clock boundaries of this daypart. Critical for multi-market broadcast operations where the same daypart definition must be applied across different time zones for network affiliates and regional channels.
reference: IANA Time Zone Database; ATSC A/65; Ericsson MediaFirst Playout

description: The timestamp of the most recent modification to this daypart record. Used for change data capture (CDC), incremental ETL processing in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer, and audit trail compliance.
reference: SOX Section 404 (Internal Controls); GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

description: Indicates whether ad inventory within this daypart is offered during the upfront advance advertising sales event. Prime Time and key dayparts are typically upfront-eligible. Drives Salesforce Media Cloud opportunity and proposal configuration for annual upfront sales cycles.
reference: IAB Digital Video Ad Impression Measurement Guidelines; Salesforce Media Cloud

Accredited methodologies carry full contractual weight; conditionally accredited methodologies may have usage restrictions.
reference: Media Rating Council (MRC) Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, known limitations, special handling instructions, or contextual information about this measurement methodology. Examples include known panel biases, market-specific adjustments, or transition notes when migrating from one methodology version to another.

description: Comma-separated list of privacy and data protection frameworks under which this methodology's data collection and processing is compliant (e.g., 'GDPR, CCPA, COPPA, TCPA'). GDPR governs EU audience data; CCPA governs California viewer data; COPPA governs children's content measurement. Required for regulatory reporting and data governance.
reference: GDPR Article 5; CCPA Section 1798; COPPA 16 CFR Part 312; FCC Privacy Rules

description: The cadence at which audience measurement data is reported using this methodology: overnight (daily ratings delivery), weekly, monthly, quarterly, or sweeps_only (data available only during Nielsen Sweeps measurement periods in February, May, July, and November). Governs scheduling of ad sales reporting and programming analysis cycles.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; FCC Sweeps Period Regulations

description: The typical number of hours between the audience exposure event and the availability of processed, reportable ratings data using this methodology. reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Delivery SLA Documentation; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

description: The minimum number of panelists or measurement units required for this methodology to produce statistically valid audience estimates. reference: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; Nielsen Panel Design Specifications

description: The ideal or design target number of panelists or measurement units for this methodology to achieve the desired statistical confidence level and margin of error. Used in panel management and methodology performance monitoring against MRC accreditation benchmarks.
reference: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; Nielsen Panel Design Specifications

description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this methodology definition originates (e.g., 'NIELSEN_MRP' for Nielsen Media Research Platform, 'ADOBE_AEP' for Adobe Experience Platform). description: The calendar date on which the program episode aired on the specified channel and market. Used as the principal business event date for this measurement record.

description: The precise date and time at which the program finished airing. Combined with air_start_time to derive program duration for audience measurement calculations.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Ericsson MediaFirst Playout

description: The precise date and time (including timezone offset) at which the program began airing. Used for exact scheduling alignment and daypart classification.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Ericsson MediaFirst Playout

description: The percentage of the program's total audience represented by the primary target demographic (typically A18-49). Indicates how well the program indexes against its target audience and is used in ad sales proposals and programming strategy.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Composition Standards

description: The average number of persons or households tuned to the program during an average minute of the telecast. Expressed in thousands (000s). AA is the primary audience volume metric used in GRP and CPM calculations for ad sales.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Average Audience (AA) Metric

description: The unduplicated number of different persons or households that tuned to the program for at least one minute across all airings within a defined period. Expressed in thousands (000s). Cume measures total reach and is critical for frequency management in ad campaign planning.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Cumulative Audience (Cume) Metric

description: The percentage of Adults aged 18-49 in the measured universe who were tuned to this program. A18-49 is the most commercially valuable and widely traded demographic in US television advertising, serving as the primary currency for primetime ad sales.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Adults 18-49 (A18-49) Demographic Standard

description: The percentage of Adults aged 25-54 in the measured universe who were tuned to this program. A25-54 is a key secondary demographic used in news programming, cable networks, and certain advertiser categories.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Adults 25-54 (A25-54) Demographic Standard

description: The percentage of Children aged 2-11 in the measured universe who were tuned to this program. K2-11 is the primary demographic for children's programming and toy/food advertisers. Subject to COPPA compliance requirements for data handling.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Children 2-11 (K2-11) Demographic Standard; COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act)

description: The percentage of Men aged 18-49 in the measured universe who were tuned to this program. M18-49 is a primary demographic for sports, automotive, and technology advertisers.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Men 18-49 (M18-49) Demographic Standard

description: The percentage of Women aged 18-49 in the measured universe who were tuned to this program. W18-49 is a primary demographic for lifestyle, beauty, and household product advertisers.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Women 18-49 (W18-49) Demographic Standard

description: The average number of times a unique person or household was exposed to the program within the measurement period. Frequency = GRP / Reach. Used with reach for ad campaign effectiveness analysis and makegoods calculations.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Reach and Frequency Standards

description: The sum of all ratings delivered by an advertising schedule or program, representing total audience delivery without deduplication. GRP = Reach × Frequency. A fundamental currency metric in ad sales negotiations, upfront deals, and scatter market transactions.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB GRP Standard; MRC

description: The percentage of all television households in the measured universe that were tuned to this program during the measurement period. Expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 5.2 = 5.2%). The foundational Nielsen rating metric used for ad pricing and programming evaluation.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC (Media Rating Council) Minimum Standards

description: The percentage of households using television (HUT) that were tuned to this program. Share = (Program Audience / HUT) × 100. Measures competitive performance relative to active TV viewers at the same time.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Media Rating Research

description: The percentage of all television households in the universe that had their television sets in use during the measurement period. HUT is the denominator for household share calculations and a key indicator of overall TV viewing activity.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — HUT (Homes Using Television) Standard

description: The total number of person-level exposures to the program, calculated as average audience multiplied by the number of airings. Expressed in absolute numbers (not thousands). Impressions are the transactional currency for digital and cross-platform ad sales.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Impression Measurement Guidelines; MRC

description: The timestamp at which this Nielsen rating record was ingested into the Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer from the Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used for data freshness monitoring, SLA tracking, and audit trail.
reference: Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards; Nielsen Media Research Platform SLA

description: The timestamp of the most recent update to this rating record in the Silver layer, reflecting revisions from Nielsen (e.g., preliminary to final, or restated ratings). Supports change tracking and downstream consumer notification.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

description: Nielsen Media Research Platform's proprietary alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the program title within the Nielsen measurement system. Used as the business identifier for cross-referencing ratings data with Nielsen deliverables.

The date on which Nielsen Media Research officially published or delivered this rating record to the broadcaster. Distinguishes the measurement air date from the data delivery date, which is critical for tracking preliminary vs. final rating release cycles.

The ISO 8601 week identifier (e.g., 2024-W23) of the Nielsen measurement week in which this rating was reported. Nielsen measurement weeks run Monday through Sunday. Used for weekly ratings aggregation and trend analysis.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; ISO 8601 Week Date Standard

description: The percentage of all persons in the measured universe who were watching television during the measurement period. PUT is the denominator for persons share calculations and complements HUT for demographic audience analysis.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — PUT (Persons Using Television) Standard

description: Lifecycle status of this Nielsen rating record indicating whether the data is preliminary (fast nationals), final, or has been revised. Ad sales and programming decisions must distinguish preliminary from final ratings. Preliminary ratings are typically released within 24 hours; final ratings follow within days.

The unduplicated number of unique persons or households exposed to the program at least once within the measurement period. Expressed in thousands (000s). Reach is a core metric for ad campaign planning and audience delivery reporting.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Reach and Frequency Standards

description: The native record identifier assigned by the Nielsen Media Research Platform for this rating record. Preserved in the Silver layer for data lineage, reconciliation, and re-ingestion traceability back to the authoritative source system.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Data Lineage Best Practices

description: Indicates whether this rating was measured during a Nielsen Sweeps period (February, May, July, November intensive measurement periods). Sweeps ratings carry elevated importance for affiliate compensation, ad rate setting, and programming strategy.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Sweeps Measurement Periods

description: The average number of minutes that viewers in the measured audience spent watching the program. A key engagement metric used in programming decisions and content performance analysis. Expressed in minutes.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Time Spent Viewing (TSV) Metric

description: The total number of persons or households that tuned to the program for at least six consecutive minutes. Expressed in thousands (000s). TA provides a broader reach measure than AA and is used for program promotion and scheduling decisions.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Total Audience (TA) Metric

description: Rating points delivered specifically to a defined target demographic audience (e.g., Adults 18-49). TRP = (Target Audience Impressions / Target Universe) × 100. Used by advertisers to evaluate efficiency of reaching their specific target demographic.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — TRP (Target Rating Point) Standard; IAB

description: The total estimated number of television households in the measured market or national universe used as the denominator for household rating calculations. Expressed in thousands (000s). Nielsen updates universe estimates annually based on census data.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Universe Estimates; U.S. Census Bureau

description: The total estimated number of persons in the measured market or national universe used as the denominator for persons rating calculations. Expressed in thousands (000s). Segmented by demographic group for TRP calculations.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Universe Estimates; U.S. Census Bureau

reference: Adobe Experience Platform — Audience Segmentation; IAB Digital Audience Standards

description: Percentage of recruited panel households or individuals who are actively and consistently providing usable measurement data. A declining cooperation rate is an early indicator of panel quality degradation and may trigger MRC review. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.8500 = 85%).
reference: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement; Nielsen Panel Quality Standards

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code indicating the primary country of coverage for this panel (e.g., USA, GBR, AUS). Required for international panels and regulatory reporting to Ofcom and the European Audiovisual Observatory.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; Ofcom Broadcasting Standards; European Audiovisual Observatory

description: Timestamp when this audience panel record was first created in the lakehouse Silver layer. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for data lineage, audit trails, and compliance with SOX financial reporting controls that require traceability of audience data used in revenue recognition.
reference: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); ISO 8601

description: Technical mechanism used to collect viewing data from panel members. Electronic meters (people meters) require active button-pressing; set-top-box (STB) and smart TV ACR (Automatic Content Recognition) are passive; diary is self-reported. Determines the granularity and reliability of minute-by-minute audience data.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Data Collection Methodology; ATSC Standards; MRC Accreditation Standards

description: Narrative or structured description of the demographic breakdowns captured by this panel (e.g., 'Age 2+, Adults 18-49, Adults 25-54, Persons 2-17, Households by income quintile'). Defines which demographic cuts are available for TRP (Target Rating Point) calculations and demographic audience guarantees in ad sales.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Demographic Reporting; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

description: Date on which this panel was retired or superseded by a newer panel vintage. Null for currently active panels. Used to scope historical ratings queries to the correct panel vintage and to manage panel transitions during sweeps periods.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Lifecycle; MRC Accreditation Standards

description: Date on which this panel became the active currency measurement source for audience projections. Marks the beginning of the period for which this panel's data is used in ratings reports, ad sales guarantees, and GRP/TRP delivery calculations.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Activation; MRC Accreditation Standards

description: Breadth of geographic coverage represented by this panel. National panels project to the total US population; DMA (Designated Market Area) panels project to a specific local television market; International panels cover non-US territories.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Geographic Coverage Standards; FCC Market Definition Rules

description: Indicates whether this panel is designated as the official currency measurement source for audience guarantees in advertising transactions. True = this panel's data is used as the contractual basis for GRP/TRP delivery and makegood calculations in upfront and scatter market deals. False = supplemental or research-only panel.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Currency Designation; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

description: The lowest audience rating value (expressed as a decimal fraction of the universe) that this panel can reliably report without exceeding acceptable statistical error thresholds. Ratings below this threshold are suppressed or flagged as unreliable. Typically expressed as a percentage (e.g., 0.0010 = 0.1%). Governed by MRC minimum cell size requirements.
reference: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement; Nielsen Reporting Thresholds

description: Date on which the MRC most recently granted or renewed accreditation for this panel. Used to track accreditation currency and schedule renewal audits. Panels must maintain continuous accreditation to support upfront and scatter market ad sales guarantees.
reference: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement

business_glossary_term: Media Rating Council (MRC) Accreditation Expiry Date
description: Date on which the current MRC accreditation for this panel expires and must be renewed. Expiry triggers a mandatory re-audit process. Ad sales teams must be notified of impending expiry to manage risk on guaranteed audience delivery commitments.
reference: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement

description: Current accreditation status granted by the Media Rating Council (MRC) for this panel. MRC accreditation is the industry standard for currency-grade audience measurement. Accredited panels are required for guaranteed ad buys and upfront sales commitments. Non-accredited panels cannot be used as primary currency.
reference: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

description: Nielsen's proprietary internal identifier for this panel as maintained in the Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used for direct API integration, data feed reconciliation, and cross-referencing Nielsen ratings reports. Distinct from the internal audience_panel_id surrogate key.

description: Free-text field for capturing operational notes, known data quality issues, methodology changes, or special considerations associated with this panel (e.g., 'Sample boosted in Q3 2023 for Hispanic demographic', 'Methodology change effective Jan 2024 — includes streaming'). Used by audience analytics and ad sales teams.

description: Indicates whether this panel captures out-of-home (OOH) viewing, such as viewing in bars, hotels, airports, and other public venues. reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Out-of-Home Measurement Methodology; MRC OOH Standards

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code assigned by the measurement provider (e.g., Nielsen) to uniquely identify this panel within their system. Used for cross-system reconciliation with the Nielsen Media Research Platform.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Registry

description: Human-readable name of the audience measurement panel (e.g., 'Nielsen National People Meter 2024', 'Nielsen Local People Meter — New York DMA'). Used in reporting, dashboards, and ad sales presentations.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Registry

description: Current lifecycle state of the audience panel. Active panels are used for currency-grade audience projections. Suspended panels are temporarily halted due to quality or compliance issues. Retired panels are decommissioned and replaced by newer vintages.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Lifecycle Management; MRC Accreditation Standards

description: Classification of the audience measurement methodology used by this panel. National People Meter (NPM) and Local People Meter (LPM) are electronic metered panels; Portable People Meter (PPM) captures out-of-home exposure; Diary is self-reported; Return Path Data (RPD) is set-top-box passback data; Hybrid combines multiple methods.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Methodology Standards; MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement

description: Statistical sampling approach used to recruit panel members. Probability-based sampling (address-based or random-digit-dial) is required for MRC-accredited currency panels. Opt-in panels are used for supplemental or proprietary measurement. Affects the projectability and accreditation status of the panel.
reference: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement; Nielsen Methodology Documentation

description: Cadence at which panel membership is rotated or refreshed to prevent panel conditioning effects and maintain demographic representativeness. Annual and biennial refreshes are standard for people meter panels; continuous recruitment is used for large-scale return path data panels.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Rotation Policy; MRC Accreditation Standards

description: Finest time interval at which this panel can produce reliable audience estimates. Minute-by-minute granularity is available from electronic people meter panels and supports DAI (Dynamic Ad Insertion) optimization. Quarter-hour is standard for diary panels. Determines compatibility with EPG-based program-level ratings reporting.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Reporting Specifications; SCTE Standards

description: Estimated margin of error (as a percentage) for audience projections derived from this panel at a 95% confidence interval. Smaller panels have higher sampling error. Used by ad sales teams to communicate measurement uncertainty to advertisers and to set makegood thresholds for audience delivery shortfalls.
reference: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement; Nielsen Methodology Documentation

description: Total number of sample households actively participating in this panel at any given time. Drives the statistical reliability and margin of error of projected audience estimates. A larger panel size yields lower sampling error for low-rated programs.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Sample Design; MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement

description: Total number of individual persons (panelists) actively measured within this panel. Distinct from household count because multiple individuals per household are measured for demographic breakdowns used in Target Rating Point (TRP) calculations.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Sample Design; MRC Minimum Standards

description: Indicates whether this panel captures streaming and OTT (Over-The-Top) viewing in addition to linear broadcast. Streaming-enabled panels support cross-platform audience measurement combining linear TV, SVOD, AVOD, and FAST channel viewing for total audience reporting.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Cross-Platform Measurement; IAB Digital Measurement Guidelines

description: Indicates whether this panel is used during Nielsen Sweeps periods (February, May, July, November) for local market ratings measurement. Sweeps data drives local ad rates and program scheduling decisions. Only MRC-accredited panels with sufficient local market sample sizes are sweeps-eligible.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Sweeps Methodology; FCC Local Market Rules

description: Total projected population size (in persons or households) that this panel is designed to represent. The universe estimate is the denominator used to convert raw panel viewing counts into ratings percentages (e.g., HUT, PUT, Share). Updated periodically based on census data.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Universe Estimates; US Census Bureau; MRC Accreditation Standards

description: Specifies whether the universe_estimate represents total households, total persons, or TV households (HUT-eligible). TV households are the standard denominator for HUT (Homes Using Television) calculations in broadcast ratings.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Universe Methodology; MRC Standards

description: Timestamp when this audience panel record was most recently modified in the lakehouse Silver layer. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used to detect stale panel configurations and trigger downstream recalculation of audience projections dependent on this panel.
reference: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); ISO 8601

description: Calendar year in which this panel sample was designed and recruited. Panels are periodically refreshed to maintain demographic representativeness as the population changes. Vintage year is used to track panel age and schedule mandatory refreshes per MRC accreditation requirements.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Refresh Cycle; MRC Accreditation Standards

description: Numeric multiplier applied to this panel's raw viewing data to project sample observations to the total universe estimate. A weighting factor greater than 1.0 indicates the panel under-represents a demographic segment relative to the population. Used in GRP and TRP calculations.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Projection Methodology; MRC Standards

description: Description of the statistical weighting approach applied to panel data to correct for demographic imbalances and non-response bias (e.g., 'Iterative Proportional Fitting / Raking', 'Post-stratification weighting by age/sex/race/income'). Critical for ensuring projected audience estimates are representative of the total population.
reference: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Weighting Methodology; MRC Accreditation Standards

description: Start date of the current accrual period (e.g., calendar year, fiscal year, or anniversary year depending on Media Broadcasting policy).
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Module - Time Quota Period

description: Rate at which leave accrues per pay period or per hour worked, based on employee tenure and policy tier. Expressed in hours or days per unit time.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Module - Time Quota Accrual Rate

description: The date as of which this leave balance snapshot is accurate. Typically updated at the end of each pay period or after a leave transaction.

description: Leave balance carried forward from the prior accrual period. Subject to carryover caps per Media Broadcasting policy (e.g., maximum 40 hours vacation carryover).

reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Module - Time Quota Carryover Limit

description: Timestamp when this leave balance record was first created in the system. Audit trail for record lifecycle.
reference: Internal Data Management Standard - Audit Trail

description: Current eligibility status of the employee for this leave type. Ineligible may apply during probation, leave of absence, or termination notice period.

description: Leave hours or days forfeited at the end of the prior period due to exceeding carryover caps or use-it-or-lose-it policy. Represents lost leave liability.

description: Indicates whether this leave balance record is currently active. Inactive records represent historical snapshots or terminated leave types.
Date of the most recent leave accrual transaction for this employee and leave type. Typically aligns with pay period end date.

description: Date of the most recent leave usage (deduction) for this employee and leave type. Helps identify stale balances and usage patterns.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Module - Last Absence Date

description: Code representing the type of leave (e.g., VAC for vacation, SICK for sick leave, PTO for paid time off, FLOAT for floating holiday, COMP for compensatory time). Standardized codes per Media Broadcasting HR policy.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Module - Absence Type

description: Human-readable name of the leave type (e.g., Vacation, Sick Leave, Personal Time Off, Floating Holiday, Compensatory Time).
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Module - Absence Type Text

description: Free-text notes regarding this leave balance record, including reasons for manual adjustments, policy exceptions, or special circumstances documented by HR.

reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Module - Pending Absence Requests

description: The accrual policy tier applicable to this employee for this leave type, typically based on tenure or job level (e.g., Tier 1: 0-2 years, Tier 2: 3-5 years, Tier 3: 6+ years).
reference: Media Broadcasting HR Policy Manual - Leave Accrual Tiers

description: Forecasted leave balance at the end of the current accrual period, assuming no further usage. Used for liability planning and to alert employees of potential forfeitures.
reference: Media Broadcasting HR Analytics - Leave Liability Forecast

description: Unit in which leave balance is tracked and reported: hours or days. Standardized per leave type and employee classification.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Module - Time Unit

description: User ID or system identifier of the person or process that last updated this leave balance record. Supports audit and compliance requirements.
Timestamp when this leave balance record was last modified. Updated each pay period or after leave transactions. Audit trail for record lifecycle.

reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Module - Time Quota Deduction

Identifier of the employee submitting the leave request. Links to the employee master record in the workforce domain.
Identifier of the employee designated to cover the absent employee's responsibilities during the leave period. Null if no formal substitute assigned.
Actual number of leave days taken, calculated from time and attendance records. Used for leave balance deduction and payroll processing.

Actual number of leave hours taken, calculated from time and attendance records. Used for hourly leave balance deduction and payroll processing.
Actual first date the employee was absent on approved leave. May differ from requested start date if employee returned early or extended leave.
Date when the approving manager made the approval or denial decision. Null if request is still pending.

Current lifecycle status of the leave request: pending (awaiting manager review), approved (manager approved), denied (manager rejected), cancelled (approved but later cancelled by manager), withdrawn (employee withdrew before approval decision).
Precise timestamp when the approving manager made the approval or denial decision, including time zone. Used for audit trail and SLA tracking.
Free-text comments or notes provided by the employee when submitting the leave request, such as reason for leave or special circumstances.
Cost center code to which the employee's time is charged. Used for financial reporting and labor cost allocation during leave periods.

business_glossary_term: FMLA (Family and Medical Leave Act) Certification Date

description: Status of required medical certification for FMLA leave: not_required (non-FMLA leave), pending (certification requested but not yet received), received (certification submitted by employee), approved (HR approved certification), insufficient (certification does not meet requirements).

business_glossary_term: FMLA (Family and Medical Leave Act) Protected Flag

Timestamp when this leave request record was last updated in the system. Tracks changes to approval status, actual dates, or other fields.
Employee's remaining leave balance in days or hours after this request was approved and taken. Used for leave accrual and entitlement tracking.
Employee's available leave balance in days or hours before this request was approved and taken. Snapshot for audit and balance tracking.

description: Free-text comments or notes provided by the approving manager when reviewing the leave request, such as approval conditions or coverage arrangements.

Indicates whether this leave request involves a reduced work schedule (working fewer hours per day or days per week) rather than full-day absences. Common for FMLA return-to-work transitions.
Date when the employee submitted the leave request. Represents the principal business event timestamp for this transaction.

Last date of the requested leave period. Employee intends to return to work the following business day.
First date of the requested leave period. Employee intends to be absent starting this date.
Total number of leave days requested, calculated as business days between start and end dates. May include fractional days for partial-day leave.
Total number of leave hours requested, used for hourly leave tracking and partial-day absences. Supports intermittent FMLA leave measured in hours.

Unique identifier for the timesheet record. Primary key.

User identifier of the person who last modified this timesheet record. Used for audit trail and accountability.
The date on which the timesheet was approved by the manager. Null if not yet approved.
Current approval state of the timesheet in the workflow. Tracks progression from draft through submission, approval, or rejection.
The precise date and time when the timesheet was approved, used for audit trail and SLA tracking.
Cost center code to which the timesheet hours are allocated for financial reporting and departmental cost tracking.

Total number of on-call hours during the pay period. Relevant for broadcast engineers and technical staff required to be available for emergency playout or transmission issues.

Human-readable business identifier for the timesheet, typically formatted as TS-YYYYMMDD or similar pattern for external reference and reporting.
Total number of hours approved by the manager for payroll processing. May differ from submitted hours if adjustments were made during approval.
Total number of hours submitted by the employee across all categories (regular, overtime, double-time, on-call, shift differential, PTO, holiday, unpaid leave). Sum of all hour types.

Code identifying the labor union to which the employee belongs, if applicable. Critical for applying correct overtime rules, shift differentials, and residual calculations per union collective bargaining agreements.
Total number of unpaid leave hours recorded in this timesheet period, such as unpaid personal leave or leave without pay.
Work order number associated with the timesheet, used for tracking time against specific maintenance, production, or operational tasks.

Foreign key linking to scheduling.daypart. Business justification: Broadcast work schedules align with dayparts (morning shift covers morning daypart, prime time shift covers prime daypart). 24/7 operations shift planning requires mapping work schedules to broadcast
Identifier linking to the work scheduling daypart

Date when this work schedule pattern is no longer active. Null for currently active schedules. Used to retire outdated schedules while preserving historical assignments.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Master Data Standards

description: Date when this work schedule pattern becomes active and available for employee assignment. Supports versioning and historical tracking of schedule changes.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Master Data Standards

description: FLSA classification for employees on this schedule: exempt (salaried, not eligible for overtime) or non_exempt (hourly, eligible for overtime). Determines overtime calculation and minimum wage requirements.
reference: Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA); SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll

description: Indicates whether employees on this schedule are expected to work on company-recognized holidays. True for essential broadcast operations (playout, master control), false for administrative roles.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Time Management; Collective Bargaining Agreements

description: Username or employee identifier of the person who last modified this work schedule record. Supports accountability and audit requirements.
reference: Internal Data Management Standard; SOX Compliance

description: Timestamp when this work schedule record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

Indicates whether a meal break is legally or contractually required for this schedule. True for shifts exceeding a certain duration (typically 6+ hours), false for shorter shifts. Ensures compliance with labor regulations.
reference: Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA); State Labor Laws; SAP S/4HANA HR Time Management

description: Frequency of on-call duty for schedules that include on-call rotation: none (no on-call), weekly (one week per rotation), biweekly (one week every two weeks), monthly (one week per month), as_needed (ad-hoc). Relevant for broadcast engineering and technical support roles.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Time Management; Collective Bargaining Agreements

description: Maximum time in minutes an on-call employee must respond to a call-out (e.g., 30 for 30-minute response, 60 for one-hour response). Null for schedules without on-call duty. Critical for broadcast continuity and Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance.
reference: Service Level Agreement (SLA); SAP S/4HANA HR Time Management

description: Basis for calculating overtime: daily (hours beyond threshold in a single day), weekly (hours beyond threshold in a work week), biweekly (hours beyond threshold in a two-week pay period). Determines when premium pay rates apply.
reference: Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA); SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll

description: Number of hours per day or week after which overtime compensation applies for employees on this schedule. Typically 8 hours per day or 40 hours per week under FLSA; may vary by jurisdiction and collective bargaining agreements.
reference: Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA); SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll

description: Total duration of paid breaks during the shift, measured in minutes (e.g., 15 for two 15-minute breaks). Separate from unpaid meal breaks; included in compensable time.
reference: Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA); SAP S/4HANA HR Time Management

description: Indicates whether employees assigned to this schedule must hold a valid broadcast engineering or operator license (e.g., FCC General Radiotelephone Operator License). True for technical playout and transmission roles, false for administrative and production roles.

Minimum number of hours required between the end of one shift and the start of the next for employees on this schedule (e.g., 8 for eight-hour rest, 11 for eleven-hour rest). Ensures compliance with labor regulations and employee well-being, especially for rotating broadcast shifts.
reference: Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA); State Labor Laws; European Working Time Directive; SAP S/4HANA HR Time Management

description: Number of days in the rotation cycle for rotating shift schedules (e.g., 7 for weekly rotation, 14 for bi-weekly, 28 for four-week cycle). Null for fixed schedules. Broadcast operations often use 7, 14, or 21-day cycles to ensure equitable distribution of overnight and weekend shifts.
Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the schedule pattern (e.g., STD-9TO5, SHIFT-AM, SHIFT-PM, ONCALL-ROT). Used for quick reference in HR systems and employee assignments.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Master Data Standards

description: Detailed description of the work schedule pattern, including any special conditions, rotation details, or operational notes (e.g., 'Four 10-hour shifts Monday-Thursday with Friday off; on-call rotation every fourth week; requires FCC license').

description: Human-readable name of the work schedule pattern (e.g., Standard Office Hours, Morning Broadcast Shift, Evening Playout Shift, On-Call Rotation, Compressed Work Week).
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Master Data Standards

reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Master Data Standards

description: Classification of the schedule pattern: fixed (consistent daily hours), rotating (shifts that change on a cycle), on_call (availability-based), compressed (longer days, fewer days per week), flexible (variable start/end within boundaries), split_shift (two separate work periods in one day).

Indicates whether employees on this schedule are eligible for shift differential pay (premium compensation for evening, night, or weekend shifts). True for overnight broadcast shifts, false for standard daytime office schedules.

description: Percentage or flat amount of additional compensation for shift differential, if applicable (e.g., 10 for 10% premium, 2.50 for $2.50/hour premium). Null if shift_differential_eligible is false.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll; Collective Bargaining Agreements

Standard start time for the work shift in HH:MM 24-hour format (e.g., 09:00 for 9 AM, 22:00 for 10 PM). For rotating or flexible schedules, this represents the primary or earliest start time.

IANA time zone identifier for the schedule (e.g., America/New_York, America/Los_Angeles, Europe/London). Critical for broadcast operations spanning multiple time zones to ensure accurate shift timing and playout coordination.

description: Total number of hours per week defined by this schedule pattern. Standard full-time is typically 40 hours; broadcast operations may have 37.5, 40, or 42 hours depending on shift structure and break policies.

reference: Collective Bargaining Agreements; SAP S/4HANA HR Organizational Management

description: Indicates whether this schedule includes regular weekend work (Saturday and/or Sunday). True for broadcast operations requiring 24/7 coverage, false for standard Monday-Friday office schedules.
